tool_input.description: Probe non-lenient calendar behavior with out-of-range fields

result:
I wrote `FastDateParserAgentTest` (same package, self-contained, JUnit 5) covering: basic/datetime parsing, partial-prefix parsing, getters (`getPattern`/`getLocale`/`getTimeZone` defensive copy), `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`, null-argument handling, parse-failure semantics via `ParsePosition` (index unchanged, error index set, out-of-bounds start index, empty string), `parse(String, ParsePosition, Calendar)`, two-digit year century adjustment boundaries, four-digit-year non-adjustment, all four hour-pattern boundary mappings (`H`/`K`/`h`/`k`), AM/PM and month-name text fields (including case-insensitivity and invalid-name failure), quoted literals and unterminated-quote/unsupported-letter errors, RFC-822/ISO-8601/named time zones, serialization round-trip, week-year (`Y`) resolution, numeric-overflow graceful failure, and a non-US locale month name.

All 40 tests pass against the current implementation, matching the documented/expected behavior — I didn't find a bug in `FastDateParser` worth a failing test. One avenue I probed and discarded: the Javadoc on `parse(String, ParsePosition, Calendar)` claims it throws `IllegalArgumentException` for an out-of-range field on a non-lenient `Calendar`, but `Calendar.set()` validates lazily (only on `get()`/`getTime()`), so that never actually happens here — it looked like stale/inaccurate documentation rather than a parser bug, so I didn't add a test for it.
